annotations.title: Thamar.
annotations.text: Christ abhorred not to take flesh of some that were il, as he chose Iudas among his Apostles: Let not vs disdaine to receaue our spiritual birth and sustenance of such as be not alwayes good.

annotations.title: Ioseph.
annotations.text: Ioseph marying our Lady as neere of kinne (for so was the <mn>◦</mn> law) by his pedegree sheweth hers, and consequently Christs pedegree from Dauid.

annotations.title: Husband.
annotations.text: True and perfect mariage, and continual liuing in the same, without carnal copulation. Aug. lib. 2. Consen. Euang. c. 1.

annotations.title: Borne in her.
annotations.text: The triple good or perfection of mariage accomplished in the parents of Christ, to wit, Issue, Fidelitie, Sacrament. Aug. de nup. & conc. li. 1. c. 11.

annotations.title: A Virgin.
annotations.text: ◦ Our Sauiour borne in mariage, but yet of a Virgin, would honour both states: and withal, teacheth vs agaynst Iouinian the old Heretike and these of our time, that virginity and the continent life are preferred before mariage that hath carnal copulation. See S. Hierom. adu. Iouin. and S. Greg. Nazianz. Ser. 20. de studio in pauperes, in initio.

annotations.title: A Virgin.
annotations.text: As our Ladie both a virgin and a mother, brought forth Christ the head corporally: so the Churche a virgin and a mother, bringeth forth the members of this head spiritually. Aug. li. de virg. ca. 2.

annotations.title: And bring forth.
annotations.text: ◦ The Heretike Iouinian is here refuted, holding that her virginity was corrupted in bringing forth Christ. Aug. hær. 28. Li. 1 cont. Iulian. c. 2.

annotations.title: Til, First-borne.
annotations.text: ◦ Heluidius of old abused these wordes, til, and, first-borne, agaynst the perpetual virginity of our B. Ladie. Hiero. cont. Helu. Which truth though not expressed in Scripture, yet our Aduersaries also do graunt, and Heluidius for denial therof was condemned for an heretike by tradition only. Aug. hær. 84.
